text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two representatives of the World Bank arrived in Latvia, invited by Prime Minister Andris Shkele, to help the government with anti-corruption measures.

- The cabinet has approved in principle Latvia's stand in talks with Russia over mutual land borders. The concept, considered in a confidential government meeting, is not expounded by either the government or Foreign Affairs Ministry.
- Janis Apelis, a former deputy state secretary of the Interior Ministry, has been appointed head of Latvia's security police.
- Parliament's Budget and Finance Committee rejected a proposed reduction of excise tax on some beer and wines.
- The cabinet approved the draft agreement between Latvia and Denmark on abolishing visa regulations and repatriation of illegal immigrants.

- Parliament rejected amendments to the law on social ASsistance which envisaged paying social benefits to childless pensioners with small income, as well as creating mutual assistance societies by pensioners without families.
- The Latvian Privatisation Agency is to sell the state-owned shares of the Latvian Press Association, Union Baltic Bank of Ventspils and Venoil.
- Balta, the largest Baltic insurance company, expects to make its first public issue of shares next year and to seek listing in the Riga Stock EXchange.
